subject.title: [Bug]: Discord routing / mention-gating issue in OpenClaw

question: Should Discord preflight adopt strict active-target scoping that suppresses the current/default agent when another configured agent, role target, or quoted/later mention signal means the current agent is not being addressed?
rationale: The source gap is concrete, but the fix changes Discord routing precedence and role/bot-loop semantics for multi-agent guild setups, so maintainers need to choose the product contract before automation rewrites routing behavior.

options.title: Adopt strict active-target scoping
options.body: Implement Discord-owned target resolution before default routing, drop messages that target other configured agents, scope mention text to the opening attention window, and add live Discord proof.

options.title: Split into narrower issues
options.body: Keep this umbrella open only as coordination while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/13487, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/7717, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80235 own separate slices.

options.title: Keep current default-owner behavior
options.body: Document that default routing and existing ignoreOtherMentions/allowBots policies remain the contract, and close narrower requests that conflict with that behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict active-target scoping
recommendation.body: Implement Discord-owned target resolution before default routing, drop messages that target other configured agents, scope mention text to the opening attention window, and add live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current history and prior review context point to steipete across the affected Discord preflight, shared mention policy, and routing contract.
